pull_request.title: systemd: Add functions.escapeSystemdExecArg[s]

review_comments.body: There's nothing pkgs specific here. Should we move this into lib.cli ?

I assumed it was placed in `utils` because it may have to depend on `config.systemd.package` if they require more or different escaping in the future, or maybe it didn't feel "standard library" enough at the time.

@infinisil do you think this is in scope for `lib`? I feel don't feel like we should do this for any arbitrary package, but maybe `systemd` isn't any arbitrary package.
I'd also prefer this to be in lib. It's small enough, and I doubt it'll change.

there is `systemd-escape` that implements this function as a binary that ships with systemd. But the whole point of these functions was to have a pure alternative to this IIRC.

People can just call the `systemd-escape` binary in a derivation if they need it during build time instead of run time

`systemd-escape` would be nice for a non-VM property test / fuzzing.

I'll move it to `lib`.

> > maybe `systemd` isn't any arbitrary package.

Ok, I've [done](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/compare/master...roberth:nixpkgs:systemd-functions-bad) it, but as a `lib` maintainer I wouldn't accept it. Now the `lib` testing depends on NixOS? Not cool. Also it presents a slippery slope as to what the scope of `lib` even is. Didn't feel right. Wasted my time.

> There's nothing pkgs specific here. Should we move this into lib.cli ?

There's also nothing lib specific here.

> It's small enough,

Smallness is not a criterium for `lib` additions.

> and I doubt it'll change.

Famous last words.


------

So we're at an apparent impasse.
I might know a place...
Ok, so maybe https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/402298 `.systemd.something`, but I'm starting to [repeat](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/345459) myself. Am I going crazy?
We can expose it as a passthru of the `systemd` derivation if that's what you're thinking about. Also works for me.
Where is this 2 coming from? Was there a previous version and we now have another interface?
review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
+/**
+  Build the `systemd.functions` library (where `systemd` is the package)
+*/
+{ lib, systemd }:
+let
+  inherit (lib)
+    concatMapStringsSep
+    isDerivation
+    isFloat
+    isInt
+    isPath
+    isString
+    replaceStrings
+    ;
+  inherit (builtins)
+    toJSON
+    ;
+
+  /**
+    Quotes an argument for use in `Exec*` service lines.
+    Additionally we escape `%` to disallow expansion of `%` specifiers. Any lone `;`
+    in the input will be turned into `";"` and thus lose its special meaning.
+    Every `$` is escaped to `$$`, this makes it unnecessary to disable environment
+    substitution for the directive.
+  */
+  escapeSystemdExecArg =
+    arg:
+    let
+      s =
+        if isPath arg then
+          "${arg}"
+        else if isString arg then
+          arg
+        else if isInt arg || isFloat arg || isDerivation arg then
+          toString arg
+        else
+          throw "escapeSystemdExecArg only allows strings, paths, numbers and derivations";
+    in
+    # systemd accepts "-quoted strings with escape sequences, toJSON produces
+    # a subset of these.
+    replaceStrings [ "%" "$" ] [ "%%" "$$" ] (toJSON s);
+
+  /**
+    Quotes a list of arguments into a single string for use in a Exec* line.
+  */
+  escapeSystemdExecArgs = concatMapStringsSep " " escapeSystemdExecArg;
+in
+# Instead of requiring v2, we can make this library conditional on the version as needed.
+assert systemd.interfaceVersion == 2;

review_comments.body:
Not sure we absolutely need this:

I'm not confident escaping will change (at all), and especially not by someone setting `config.systemd.package` explicitly. We can probably just pull this from `pkgs.systemd`.
